query: Starting from a W–Cu composite containing W particles or interconnected W ligaments within a Cu matrix, what single intervention could overcome phase separation and interfacial void formation, thereby improving thermal conductivity relative to the untreated composite under heat-transfer and irradiation conditions relevant to joints between W-based plasma-facing materials and Cu-based cooling components? Formulate one hypothesis that states the intervention, the proposed mechanism, the predicted comparative outcome, the applicable processing and service boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Deposition of a thin nanocrystalline Ni interlayer on W surfaces prior to Cu infiltration will form a graded W–Ni–Cu diffusion zone that lowers interfacial energy, mitigates thermal expansion mismatch, and prevents void nucleation and phase separation under high heat flux and irradiation, thereby increasing the effective thermal conductivity relative to untreated W–Cu composites.
generation.material_initial_state: W–Cu composite containing W particles or interconnected W ligaments in a Cu matrix produced by pressureless Cu infiltration, without any interfacial treatment.
generation.intervention: Electrodeposition of a ~100 nm nanocrystalline Ni layer onto all exposed W surfaces before Cu infiltration, followed by liquid-phase sintering at 1000–1050 °C.
generation.conditions: Processing: sintering at 1000–1050 °C, ambient pressure; Service: heat flux up to 2 MW/m² at 400–700 °C and neutron irradiation to 1×10²² n/m² (E>0.1 MeV).
generation.structural_mediator: A continuous graded diffusion zone ~200 nm thick at the W–Cu interface enriched in Ni, forming W–Ni and Ni–Cu solid solutions.
generation.mechanism: The Ni interlayer reduces W–Cu interfacial energy and thermal expansion mismatch, provides a diffusion bridge that suppresses Kirkendall void formation and phase separation under irradiation and thermal cycling.
generation.predicted_outcome: The Ni-treated composite will exhibit ≥10% higher effective thermal conductivity and ≥50% lower interfacial void volume fraction after service conditions compared to the untreated composite.
generation.baseline: Untreated W–Cu composite shows ~150 W/m·K thermal conductivity and ~5% interfacial void volume fraction after identical service exposure.
generation.boundary: Valid for Ni interlayer thickness between 50 and 200 nm, sintering at 1000–1050 °C, service temperatures 400–700 °C, and neutron fluence up to 1×10²² n/m².
generation.uncertainty: Moderate, due to potential variability in Ni deposition quality and interdiffusion kinetics.

falsification_experiment.design: Produce two sets of W–Cu composites—one with the Ni interlayer and one without—using identical infiltration and sintering parameters. Expose both sets to the specified heat flux, thermal cycling, and neutron irradiation.
measurements: Interfacial void volume fraction determined by SEM tomography
Effective thermal conductivity measured by laser flash analysis at 600 °C before and after irradiation
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Ni-treated composite fails to show both ≥10% increase in thermal conductivity and ≥50% reduction in interfacial void volume fraction relative to the untreated composite, the hypothesis is falsified.
